title: Env Bool
statement: Implement `solve(text)`. Interpret an environment-style string. After strip and casefold, `1`, `true`, `yes`, and `on` return 1. `0`, `false`, `no`, `off`, and the empty string return 0. Any other text returns the string `error`. The word `false` must not count as true just because the string is non-empty.
hints: Strip and casefold before the membership tests.
Check the true set and the false set separately.
A non-empty unrecognized word is error, not 1.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: bool("false") is true in Python because the string is non-empty.

editorial: bool("false") is true in Python because the string is non-empty. Environment flags are a different language. The recognized words are a closed set, and everything else is a configuration error rather than a silent true.
